To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effects of word length on lexical decision are U shaped, with facilitatory effects for 3- to 5-letter words, null effects for 6- to 8-letter words, and inhibitory effects for 9- to 13-letter words.
the effect of number of syllable on lexical decision was facilitatory for monosyllabic words, null for bisyllabic words, and inhibitory (i.e., slowing of response time) for polysyllabic words.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of number of letters in visual word recognition.
the effect of number of orthographic letters on the lexical decision response time.
the effect of word-length on the time required to recognize printed words.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of word-length on visual word recognition is a complex phenomenon that is dependent on a number of factors.
the word length effect is a complex phenomenon that depends on word length, word frequency, number of neighbors, and number of syllables.
the effect of word frequency in visual word recognition is a very complicated matter and is likely to vary as a function of a number of different factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are multiple factors contributing to the word length effect and that these factors interact in complex ways.
there are at least two independent length effects in visual word recognition.

the word length effect is not a simple function of the number of letters, but is a more complex function that depends on other variables, including number of syllables and printed frequency, and is also dependent upon the number of orthographic and phonological neighbors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the word length effect is a complex phenomenon that is not easily accounted for by current models of visual word processing.
there is a need for models to explain the U-shaped pattern of results.
word length is not a simple linear predictor.
